subject: MSA: proposed audit sprint + SOC 2 rollback clauses
messages:
From: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@medgroup.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA draft — audit/inspection language questions

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA. A few follow-ups from our side on the security exhibit and inspection rights so Legal can finish redlines:

- SOC 2: we require confirmation of Type II coverage for the last 12 months and prefer quarterly evidence pushes (summary report + exception log). Can you confirm cadence?
- Pen test access: request is for a 30-day notice window plus an agreed staging environment. We also need a point of contact for on-call during the window.
- Scoped inspections: can you propose a bounded inspection band rather than unlimited sampling (we're OK with limited sampling + a remediation checkpoint).

Also, our GC asked whether Redwood would accept a narrow "rollback" clause: if a failing control is identified in SOC 2 for two consecutive quarters, we need either a remediation plan or temporary cessation of data-sensitive calls until mitigated. Is that something your security/Legal team would accept?

Can you and your ops/legal folks propose language and an evidence rhythm we can circulate? We have procurement review on Friday.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Emily
Emily Sanders
Sr. Manager, Security & Compliance
MedGroup Health
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@medgroup.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA draft — audit/inspection language questions

Emily —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below; attaching a first-pass redline to start the negotiation.

Summary responses:
- SOC 2 cadence: Redwood can provide the last 12 months of Type II attestations and a quarterly high-level control summary (PDF) plus a short exception log. For full artifacts we propose a scheduled evidence sprint (45-60 minute review call) per quarter.
- Pen test: 30-day notice is reasonable. We'll include staging access specifics in the security exhibit: ephemeral creds, scoped IPs, and a single on-call contact (we'll nominate an infra lead).
- Scoped inspections: we prefer a bounded inspection band (e.g., up to 3 sampled systems per 12-month period) with an agreed escalation path.

On the rollback clause: we want to avoid automatic cessation language. Proposed alternative (see attached redline): a two-step remediation ladder — (1) mandatory remediation plan within 30 days, (2) if unresolved after 90 days, temporary mitigation measures (rate-limiting or scoped isolation) rather than wholesale halt. We included a short "business continuity carveout" to allow customer continuity while we remediate.

Next steps:
- Monica, Laura: skim the attached redline and flag any legal must-haves before I share back with MedGroup.
- Emily: if Procurement needs a one-pager mapping our proposed cadence to their request, I can produce that today.

Attaching: MSA_redline_proposal_v1.docx; SOC2-report-summary-2026.pdf

Thanks,
Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA draft — audit/inspection language questions

Looping in legal context from my side — please see inline highlights in the attached redline. Key legal asks I want visible to MedGroup:

- Limit sampling to the minimal set and require MedGroup to provide a short rationale for any additional scope beyond the agreed band.
- Replace any "suspension"/"cessation" language with conditional mitigation steps; we can accept the remediation ladder Rohan proposed but add defined SLA windows for remediation deliverables.
- Add an owner and contact info section for the pen-test window (we'll provide a named on-call and escalation matrix).

If MedGroup insists on remediation-triggered suspension, we should add a short dispute-resolution timeline (15 business days) and a predefined fallback model (temporary rate limits + data routing to an alternate cluster) so customer operations are not disrupted.

I recommend we send the edited redline and a 1-page "audit cadence table" that maps: quarterly summary + sprint call, full artifact by request with 10 business days' turnaround, and pen-test notice 30 days.

Monica
Monica Patel
Security & Compliance Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@medgroup.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: MedGroup Legal <legal@medgroup.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA draft — audit/inspection language questions

Thanks — that all looks workable. Two quick asks before we close:

1) Can Redwood commit to the 10-business-day turnaround for requested artifacts (we can make the request via secure GDrive link)?
2) For the remediation ladder, can you add a bullet that guarantees a monthly status update to MedGroup security while the remediation is open?

If you can confirm those two items I will escalate the redline to our GC and procurement and aim to return a signed order form by next Wednesday.

Appreciate the collaboration — happy to do the 20-minute call you offered if anything stalls.

Emily
